newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese pound continues rise against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese pound continues rise against dollar.

text.p: The Lebanese pound continued its rise against the U.S. dollar in a quiet market in the week ended on Friday, and dealers said there was no exceptional activity on the market.

The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band during the week to 1,543-1,552 pounds per dollar from 1,543.5-1,553, with the dollar trading at the bottom of the band throughout the week, dealers said.
Talal Abou Zaki, manager of forex and money market for Bank of Beirut and the Arab Countries, said trade was restricted to a tight range of 50 to 75 piastres at the bid end of the intervention band.
Commercial banks took most of the dollar offers. There were few orders for dollars by investors whose Lebanese pound-denominated treasury bills had matured and did not want to by new bills.

"There was nothing exceptional in the market, the few demand orders for dollars was caused by foreign investors who did not want to buy other t-bills after earlier ones matured, and those orders were met," Abou Zaki said.
